newsitem.title: UK: Shares fall as UK scraps tax credits on buybacks.
newsitem.headline: Shares fall as UK scraps tax credits on buybacks.

text.p: Britain's stock market took a sharp dive on Tuesday after the government said shareholders would no longer be able to claim tax credits on share buybacks or special dividend payouts.
The surprise statement wiped almost 30 points off the Financial Time/Stock Exchange index of 100 leading shares but it then steadied to 4,009.7 compared with a previous close of 4,031.5.
Shares in Reuters Holdings Plc and other companies planning or likely to make share buybacks or special dividend payments showed the greatest losses.
Reuters, which announced plans for a 613 million sterling ($957.7 million) bonus share issue in September, initially fell 23p to 753-1/2 pence.
Other companies in a strong cash position were also lower, with Great Universal Stores Plc down 17-1/2p at 609 and Barclays Plc down 21p at 953-1/2.
Bank and utility stocks were seen as among the biggest casualties of the Treasury ruling.

In a statement British finance minister Kenneth Clarke said the new ruling stemmed from "...the growing loss of tax through schemes involving companies buying their own shares or paying special dividends..."
He said a provision would be included in the next Finance Bill to change the tax treatment of such schemes in certain circumstances, effective October 8.

"We have seen recently companies buying their own shares or paying special dividends in such a way that the proceeds end up almost entirely in the hands of those who are entitled to payment of a tax credit. This has costs for the Exchequer, and if action is not taken soon that cost would escalate," he said. ($ = 0.640 British Pounds Sterling)
